subject: Parachute clause & fee cushion — Order Form / Exhibit A redlines
messages:
From: Alexandra Liu <legal@brightlane.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightlane redlines — Order Form (pricing exhibit)

Neha / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft order form. Our finance and legal teams ran a redline and there are two commercial items we cannot accept in the current language without a concession: a) the "no-refund" sweep in section Exhibit A (pricing) and b) the lack of a short-term fee cushion or "parachute" if model performance falls below agreed thresholds in the first 90 days.

High-level asks:
- Add a limited refund carveout tied to SLA metrics (we propose a refundable credit equal to the fee differential over a measured 30-day window if latency/availability drops below 99.5%).
- Insert a temporary fee-cushion (we used the term "parachute") that caps customer exposure to overage true-ups for the first 90 days with a 10% buffer.

Attached: Brightlane_OrderForm_Redline_20270610.pdf with comments in Exhibit A.

Happy to hop on a call if helpful — our CFO (finance@brightlane.com) is looped for the commercial numbers.

Best,
Alexandra Liu
Legal Counsel, Brightlane Health
Attachments: Brightlane_OrderForm_Redline_20270610.pdf (PDF, redline)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Liu <legal@brightlane.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane redlines — Order Form (pricing exhibit)

Alexandra — thanks for the detailed notes and the redline. We reviewed with commercial and legal here. A few quick notes before we produce a formal redline:

1) Refund carveout: we understand the ask but want to limit it to measured SLA breaches tied to inference availability or model correctness regressions attributable to Redwood runtime (not customer prompt/label shift). Proposed: refundable credit up to 25% of monthly invoice for a single month if availability < 99.5% and we fail post-mitigation within 30 days.

2) Fee cushion / parachute: commercial is open to a temporary buffer but prefers a mechanism that maintains unit economics. We propose a 90-day "overage buffer" where overage true-ups are calculated but only 50% invoiced in the first 90 days (remainder credits against next invoice) — this avoids a straight cap which would transfer into long-term costs.

I've attached our suggested Exhibit A redline for your review — it keeps the structure but proposes specific percentages and trigger language.

Attachments: Redwood_ExhibitA_Proposed_Redline_20270612.docx (Word, tracked changes)

Can we target next-week sign-off? Marissa will handle pricing approvals on our side.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

From: Alexandra Liu <legal@brightlane.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane redlines — Order Form (pricing exhibit)

Neha / Marissa — we reviewed the proposed language. High-level response:

- The refundable credit as drafted is closer, but we need clearer measurement windows and a firm cap on the total credit per incident. Our finance team prefers a 30% monthly cap and a maximum of two incidents per rolling 12 months.
- The 50% billing of overage in the first 90 days is acceptable in principle, but we want the buffer expressed as a firm dollar or percent cap (Brightlane prefers a 10%-of-monthly-invoice cap on invoiced overage for the first 90 days).

We've annotated our counterproposals in the attached PDF. Please note that Brightlane cannot accept language that allows for undefined "true-ups" without a maximum exposure; our procurement policy requires a maximum potential liability carveout.

Attached: Brightlane_ExhibitA_Response_20270613.pdf

> (included original redline)

Best,
Alexandra

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Liu <legal@brightlane.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane redlines — Order Form (pricing exhibit)

Alexandra — appreciate the clarity on caps. A couple of technical/commercial clarifications from Redwood's side before we lock language:

1) Causes and exclusions: we will accept the availability-based refundable credit tied to Redwood runtime incidents only. We need explicit carveouts for customer-driven misconfiguration, prompt-engineered load spikes, or third-party infra outages (we propose an exclusions list in Exhibit A).

2) Measurement and mitigation: all SLA calculations will use our telemetry (console traces + uptime logs). Redwood commits to a 7-day remediation window for identified runtime defects. Credits apply only if remediation fails within that window.

3) Fee-cushion mechanics: instead of a dollar cap for the first 90 days, we can accept Brightlane's 10% monthly-invoice cap on billed overage. In exchange, Redwood requests that the 90-day period be measured from the later of (a) go-live date or (b) first invoice date.

If you can accept the exclusions and the start-of-90-day measurement, we can produce a clean Exhibit A for signature and circulate the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Partnerships, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | (650) 555-0212

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Liu <legal@brightlane.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane redlines — Order Form (pricing exhibit)

Alexandra — thanks to you and finance for the specificity. We're in alignment on the following negotiated points:

• Refund credit: limited to runtime-caused SLA breaches (availability < 99.5%), up to 30% of a single monthly invoice per incident, maximum two incidents in a rolling 12 months.
• Parachute / fee cushion: first 90 days after agreed start date — Brightlane will be billed overages but invoiced overage is capped at 10% of monthly invoice; unused overage amounts are reconciled on the next invoice (per the 50% deferral Neha proposed).
• Exclusions: explicit customer and third-party exclusions listed in Exhibit A.
• Measurement & remediation: Redwood telemetry is the measurement source; Redwood gets a 7-day remediation window before credits apply.

Next steps: we'll push a clean Exhibit A redline reflecting the agreed bullets and open a DocuSign envelope for signature. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/abcdef123456 (DocuSign envelope BL-23094).

Neha will circulate the final Exhibit A by EOD tomorrow. If Brightlane legal confirms the bullets above, we'll proceed to sign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
